A's -40 dB peaking notches leave the hum audible (13.1 dB prominence against B's 0.7). Its stack of limiters and compressors, together with dynaudnorm at g=31 and m=12, raises the room noise between phrases (the pause gap shrinks from 13.8 to 9.1 dB) and drops fidelity to 0.709, so it sounds over-processed. B uses a cleaner chain with true bandreject notches, a light expander, and moderate leveling, and it keeps the voice natural (fidelity 0.868). B's only weakness is that the drift sections still sit about 4 dB low, so the quiet parts are only partly brought up to match.

A takes the hum from 43.8 dB down to 0.7 dB and keeps fidelity up at 0.868. B still has 13.1 dB of hum, and its fidelity falls to 0.709 because it stacks limiters, sidechain ducking, two compressors and a 31 dB dynaudnorm, which over-processes the voice. B also lifts the pauses: the pause gap shrinks from 13.8 to 9.1 dB, so the room noise and echo come up. A's light gate and moderate levelling keep the pauses down (20.2 dB gap) and it sounds natural. A's one real weakness is that it evens out the drift sections less well than B (dip gap -4.4 vs -0.6 dB).

A ducks the music by 19.7 dB against B's 9.4 dB, which better matches 'drops well below the voice', and it also has the higher voice-to-music ratio (18.9 vs 17.2 dB) and hits -16.0 LUFS exactly. A gets there with a ratio-20 sidechain on a low threshold and a 450 ms release, so the music still comes back up between sentences. B's ratio of 6 at a -34 dBFS threshold is gentler and safer against pumping, but it leaves the bed noticeably present under the speech, and its tail runs about 4.5 s past the last word instead of A's 4 s.

B ducks the music by 19.7 dB against A's 9.4 dB and has the better voice-to-music ratio (18.9 vs 17.2 dB), so it actually meets the brief's 'well below the voice' and keeps the words clear. A's ducking is mild because its threshold is high and its ratio is only 6. B's tail is also timed exactly to the brief: the 4-second fade-out starts at the last word, while A swells first and ends about 4.5 s after it. Both scripts are equally robust and hit the loudness and true-peak targets, though B's -1.2 dBTP ceiling leaves less margin than A's -1.5.

A ducks the bed by 10.4 dB using a ratio-8 sidechain keyed from both voice and sting. B gets only 5.5 dB of ducking at ratio 4 and fails the ducks check. B also fails the voice_intact check and has lower voice fidelity, and its music sits further above the voice (VMR -3.5 vs -2.3). A also ends cleaner: it fades the bed over the last second, so the tail is at -59 dB. B only applies a 0.1 s master fade, which leaves the tail at -31 dB.

B ducks the bed by 10.4 dB against A's 5.5 dB and keeps the voice intact, so it passes two checks A fails. Its sidechain key also includes the sting, and the bed fades over the last second, which gives a much cleaner tail (-59 dB end peak vs A's -31 dB, where A depends on a 0.1 s fade at the very end). Both fall short on voice-above-music. B's post-loudnorm volume trim could in principle push the true peak too high without any check, but the measured -1.5 dBTP shows that didn't happen here.

A's measured output is broken where it matters most: the voice comes in at 5.75 s instead of 4 s, voice-to-music is -68 dB, voice fidelity is 0.34, and the music barely ducks (0.3 dB), so the pastor is effectively missing or unintelligible. B feeds the [voice] label into both the sidechain and the amix without an asplit. The measurements show what that did to the voice: fidelity 0.344, voice-to-music ratio -68 dB, essentially no ducking (0.3 dB) and a voice onset at 5.75 s, so B fails the core requirements. A splits the voice key properly, fades the music in at the 4 s start, ducks by about 10 dB with the voice 12.8 dB above the music, passes all 12 checks, and has better error handling. Its only weak spot is landing at -15.2 LUFS against the -16 target, which is still within 1 LU.

A puts the three lines in the right order at about 0.51, 4.87 and 10.01 s, and the voice comes through intact (fidelity 0.684). That is likely because B feeds its [voice] label into both the sidechain and the final mix without an asplit, which damages the main content of the spot. A has real faults of its own: it never ducks the music (fixed volume, 0.1 dB duck), and its single-pass loudnorm missed the target slightly at -15.6 LUFS. Still, a clean, correctly ordered voice is a much smaller fix than B's broken voice, even though B's two-pass loudness and sidechain approach is better engineered on paper.
